note: The top item of runs/next.md at the shipping size: `tools/port_profile.sh 2560 1440`, the same two lines r2026-11-10-11-gap-720p printed at 1280x720. That run read T **3.393** / X **3.277** ms over the same **249** dispatches - a barrier after every launch costs **0.116 ms** (0.47 us per dispatch, 3.4% of the pass), under the item's 0.3 ms line, so by its own definitions 720p puts the cost in the dispatches' own work and picks src/nr_graph.cpp, whose every knob is already at its measured optimum. That is why the item is stuck: the read that can move it without a word from the developer is this one, because T - X scales with the work (~0.34 ms at 1440p) and crosses the item's own 0.3 ms line. Read, in this order: (1) the card gate - gpu_before / gpu_after / idle_waited_s; BUSY before or a non-zero idle wait means quote nothing (r2026-11-10-profile-large-1080p read 17.056 ms with idle_waited_s 90.0 and is quoted nowhere for exactly that). (2) the two lines verbatim: `total T ms (sum of per-dispatch spans, 2560x1440), N dispatches, a barrier after every launch` and `production schedule (counter chaining): N dispatches, GPU X ms (min of 7, no client in the loop)`. T should land near r2026-11-08-profile-1440p's 9.714 ms scale and a T far from it (1.7x or more) is the contended-card signature, not a reading. (3) T - X, and then the same number divided by N for the per-dispatch barrier. Above ~0.3 ms the launch path is the lever and the next change is in `src/kernels.cpp`; if it stays inside the 0.03 ms noise bar at 1440p too, the barrier is settled as not the lever and the item needs a word naming either the PTX emitter or `src/serve.cpp`, both of which it excludes. The fixed-cost barrier probe and the kernel table come back in the same report and are the usual baselines (0.406-0.411 ms for 400 trivial dispatches). If the run dies with `vkQueueWaitIdle(queue_) failed: -4`, stop queueing and report the card - that is the driver, not a code question.
